blocks.title: Respiration
blocks.md: **Respiration** is the release of energy from food in living cells. Every living cell respires all the time. It is *not* the same as **breathing**, which is how air gets in and out of the lungs. **Aerobic respiration** uses oxygen and takes place in the mitochondria.

blocks.title: Without oxygen
blocks.md: **Anaerobic respiration** releases a small amount of energy without oxygen. In **muscles** during hard exercise glucose becomes **lactic acid** (which causes tiredness and cramp). In **yeast** glucose becomes **alcohol (ethanol)** and **carbon dioxide**: this is **fermentation**, used for bread, palm wine and beer.

blocks.caption: Inhaled and exhaled air (approximate).
blocks.alt: A bar chart: oxygen is about 21 percent in and 16 percent out; carbon dioxide is about 0.04 percent in and 4 percent out.

blocks.title: Breathing
blocks.md: **Breathing in**: the ribs move up and out, the **diaphragm** flattens, the chest gets bigger and air rushes in. **Breathing out**: the ribs move down, the diaphragm rises, the chest gets smaller and air is pushed out. Gas exchange happens in the tiny air sacs of the lungs (**alveoli**), which have thin walls and many capillaries.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Breathing and respiration are different things.
- Plants respire day and night.
- Limewater turns *milky* with carbon dioxide; it does not test oxygen.

blocks.title: Breaths in a minute
blocks.statement: A boy takes 15 breaths each minute and each breath moves 500 cm³ of air. How much air does he breathe in one minute?

blocks.title: After a race
blocks.statement: A girl is breathing fast after running. Explain why.
steps: Her muscles used oxygen quickly and made some lactic acid.
She needs extra oxygen to break down the lactic acid and to supply the muscles.
blocks.answer: To get more oxygen for the muscles and remove lactic acid.
